messages:
anna: Heads up — CI eval run for the new quantized-7b model shows pass@5 weirdness on the kbqa suite. Pass@5 dropped from ~0.82 to ~0.56 after the ingestion/dedupe change. Anyone seen this?

jordan: Can you paste the run id + exact command you used?

anna: run id: qrun-2026-0315-17. Command: `./eval-runner --suite kbqa --model redwood/quant-7b-v2 --seed 42 --dedupe true --num-candidates 10`

sasha_p: Two suspects: 1) dedupe/global-collapsing of candidate pool vs per-example dedupe, 2) seed handling when we shuffle before batching. We merged PR #887 that sorts examples by id before batching — that could change candidate composition.

mike: Reproduced locally. With `--seed 42 --dedupe false` pass@5 = 0.81 stable. With `--seed 42 --dedupe true` pass@5 fluctuates 0.55-0.57 across runs. Paste of failing summary: `expected pass@5 0.816, got 0.574`

anna: eval-bot reported CI failure: `metrics_consistency_test` in nightly — diff shows pass@k calculation mismatch.

jordan: Quick note on pass@k impl: we assume each example has its own candidate set; pass@k = 1 - \prod_{i=1..k} (1 - m_i/n_i) for sampling formula, or simpler exact-match counting when we have deterministic candidate lists. If we collapse candidates across examples, metric is meaningless.

sasha_p: Found it — the dedupe stage currently runs globally over the batch (it keeps unique strings across all examples) after we concatenated candidate lists for batched inference. For kbqa we need dedupe per-question only. I'll open a patch to change scope to per-example. Also adding an explicit invariant check in runner: assert sum(len(c)) == expected_total_candidates_per_example * num_examples.

mike: Also noticed exact-match is sensitive to tokenization differences after quantization: extra whitespace or different punctuation tokenization yields false negatives. Suggest adding a normalization step during ingest for exact-match/pass@k: lowercase, collapse whitespace, strip trailing punctuation for short answers. That should be opt-in per-suite.

anna: Agreed. Action items: sasha - PR to fix dedupe scoping and add invariant checks; jordan - add tokenization normalization toggle + tests; mike - add a CI smoke job that runs with `--dedupe true` + fixed seed to catch regressions; I'll monitor nightly run. :thumbsup:

{sasha_p}: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/912 (title: "fix(dedupe): scope to per-example, add invariant checks"). CC @jordan @mike

mike: Added CI workflow `ci/evals/dedupe-smoke` — runs against quant-7b-v2 nightly. Logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/4521 (failing before PR, passing on sasha's branch)

anna: Nice. Also filing a follow-up ticket to instrument BERTScore & calibration breakdowns by tokenization variant; quantization experiments trigger subtle calibration shifts. Ticket: RDW-2034.

jordan: FYI, BERTScore diffs are small and within variance, but calibration histograms flip for the high-confidence bin after quantization — keep an eye.

anna: Thanks team — reassigning to next sprint for patch QA and adding a regression test.
